proposed.explanation:
TMGH shows strong fundamental momentum that aligns well with your long-term, high-risk-tolerance profile. Verified figures indicate gross profit grew from 14,002,196,445 EGP in 2024 to 20,855,400,384 EGP in 2025 (≈49 % YoY), and consolidated EPS rose from 4.38 EGP to 6.98 EGP (≈59 % YoY). At the current price of 82.50 EGP, the trailing P/E is roughly 11.8×, which is reasonable for a company growing earnings at that pace. Return on equity (net profit 18,201,981,482 ÷ total equity 157,708,140,765) is about 11.5 %, a solid return on the capital base.

Because you hold no stocks yet, the diversification cap (no single company > 50 % of total portfolio value) limits the TMGH position to at most 50,000 EGP. At 82.50 EGP per share, that is 606 shares costing 49,995 EGP, leaving 50,005 EGP in cash. TMGH would then represent 49.995 % of the 100,000 EGP portfolio, just under the 50 % ceiling.

Caveats and risks: (1) The 2024 restated net-profit figure is marked AMBIGUOUS (auditor's stamp obscures digits), so I could not verify the exact year-on-year net-profit growth; the EPS growth is the verified proxy. (2) I have only one full year of verified income-statement data; a single year of strong growth does not guarantee a sustained trend. (3) No information on debt levels, dividend policy, sector cyclicality, or competitive position is available in the evidence provided. (4) The 87 % net-to-gross-profit ratio suggests a holding-company or financial-services structure where margins can be sensitive to market conditions. Given your 10+ year horizon and ability to absorb drawdowns, a measured entry at this valuation is reasonable, but the position is capped by the diversification rule and the limited evidence base. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
